$comment: Rust sysroot crates statically linked into the shipped xcframework.
WHY THIS EXISTS. `cargo tree` reports zero of these: they come from the precompiled
rust-std that the toolchain ships, not from Cargo.lock, so the generated notices have
never mentioned them. Naming them here lets --verify-committed reconcile the crates
actually present in the committed archives against the crates the notices cite, without
reporting every sysroot crate as an unattributed finding.
THIS IS AN INVENTORY, NOT AN ATTRIBUTION. Listing a crate here says only 'the archive is
expected to contain this, and the reconciliation should not flag it as unknown'. It does
NOT mean the licence obligation is discharged — 17 of these still have no notice text at
all. That work is tracked separately; see the licence corpus PR.
HOW THE SET WAS ESTABLISHED. Every `<crate>-<16hex>` member of each slice was matched
against `lib<crate>-<16hex>.rlib` in `lib/rustlib/<target>/lib` of the pinned toolchain.
Exactly these 19 match, per slice, and the NAME set is byte-identical across all three
slices (the hashes differ per target, as they must). Checked in both directions: nothing
listed here is absent from the archives, and nothing in the archives that resolves to a
KEYED ON THE TOOLCHAIN. A toolchain bump can change this set. `toolchain` is the pin this
was derived from; if rust-toolchain.toml moves and this file does not, the reconciliation
is being run against a stale inventory.
